'''Simone Techert''' is an X-ray physicist and physicochemist. She develops methods for time-resolved X-ray experiments to illuminate chemical molecular processes for example 'filming' chemical reactions in real time.

== Biography ==
Techert studied chemistry from 1988 to 1993 at the [[University of Giessen]]. She graduated in 1994. She finished her doctorate at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry]] in Göttingen in 1997. The title of her doctoral thesis was "Spectroscopy and charge separation. Theoretical and experimental studies on pyrene derivatives".<ref>{{Cite web|title=PD Dr. Simone Techert - AcademiaNet|url=https://www.academia-net.org/profil/pd-dr-simone-techert/1134068|website=www.academia-net.org|access-date=27 May 2020}}</ref>

Afterwards, she worked as a scientist at the [[European Synchrotron Radiation Facility]] (ESRF) in [[Grenoble]], until she returned to the Max Planck Institute as a group leader in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Simone Techert|url=https://www.mpibpc.mpg.de/354325/simone_techert_cv|website=www.mpibpc.mpg.de|language=en|access-date=27 May 2020}}</ref> She was the head of the Minerva group from 2006 to 2012. She has been a professor of physical chemistry since 2004. Since 2008 she has been a lecturer at the International Research School for Molecular [[Biophysics]] at the Göttingen Research Campus. In 2013, she became a professor at the [[University of Göttingen]] with a connection to the [[Helmholtz Association]] and the [[DESY|German Electron Synchrotron]] (DESY) in Hamburg. She is a Leading Scientist in the group "Chemical Structural Dynamics" at DESY.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Simone Techert|url=https://www.desy.de/about_desy/lead_scientists/simone_techert/index_eng.html|website=www.desy.de|language=en|access-date=27 May 2020}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* 1999: "Prime de Performance" award of the "European Synchrotron Radiation Facility" (ESRF)
* 2001–2004: [[Emmy Noether]] grant from the German Research Foundation
* 2002–2006: Karl Winnacker grant from the Aventis Foundation
* 2005: X-ray prize from the Liebig University Gießen for ultrashort dynamics in organic solids with time-resolved X-rays.<ref>{{Cite web|title=List of Winners of the Roentgen Prize|url=https://www.uni-giessen.de/org/admin/stab/stf/dl/preise/roentgen-preis-en/spreadsheet-en|website=Justus-Liebig-Universität Gießen|language=en|access-date=27 May 2020}}</ref>
* 2007: Bronze medal in the chemical industry
* 2013: Morino Lectureship

== Research area ==
Techert conducts research in the field of physical chemistry. She has specialized in time-resolved methods in X-ray physics, time-resolved structure determination and [[time-resolved spectroscopy]]. At DESY she works with her research group on the structural dynamics of chemical systems, especially the development of time-resolved X-ray experiments, their application and optimization for the investigation of elementary chemical processes and structure-dynamic relationships in chemical reactions, ie the "filming" of chemical reactions in real time. Her research team succeeded in 2010 in using the radiation from a [[free-electron laser]] to investigate chemical reactions.<ref>{{cite web|title=X-ray flashes "film" molecular switches|url=http://www.goettinger-tageblatt.de/Campus/Goettingen/Roentgenblitze-filmen-molekulare-Schalter|last=|first=|date=|year=|website=|publisher=|pages=|language=|format=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=13 August 2016|quote=|periodical=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Deciphered the reaction kinetics of iron pentacarbonyl|url=https://www.analytik-news.de/Presse/2015/203.html|last=|first=|date=8 April 2015|website=|publisher=analytik-news.de|pages=|language=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=24 June 2017|quote=|periodical=}}</ref> She worked on the experimental recording of hydrogen bonds as part of the Helmholtz working group.<ref>{{cite web|title=The measurement of chemistry: experimentally recorded hydrogen bonds|url=https://idw-online.de/de/news648080|last=|first=|date=|year=|publisher=|pages=|language=|format=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=23 August 2016|quote=|periodical=Idw-online.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Measuring chemistry: Local fingerprint of hydrogen bonding captured in experiments|url=http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2016-03/hbfm-mc031716.php|website=EurekAlert!|language=en|access-date=27 May 2020}}</ref> In 2017 her research (with collaborators) using time-resolved x-ray methods, laid the foundation for a new type of solar cell.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scientists lay foundations for new type of solar cell|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2017-01/ded-slf012417.php|website=EurekAlert!|language=en|access-date=27 May 2020}}</ref>
